PUBLIC RESPONSE: C

Group1: miR-139-3p, miR-186, miR-339-3p, miR-486, miR-511, miR-672, mR-708
Group2: miR-127, miR-133a, miR-145, miR-146b, miR-16, miR-221, miR-28
Group3: miR-106b*, miR-27a*, miR-15a, miR-182, miR-203, miR-204, miR-485-3p, miR-224

The expression table shows a clear loss-of-signal cluster in D10 and D21. miR-139-3p, miR-186, miR-339-3p, miR-486, miR-511, miR-672 and mR-708 are essentially zero in both D10 replicates and D21 replicates after being detectable in NonArt, and they map to the extreme negative PCA1 tail with PCA1 ≈ -15 to -20 and PCA2 ≈ +5 to +10. That is a coherent down-regulated/lost miRNA module and makes a natural Group1.

The remaining miRNAs separate on PCA1/PCA2. A high PCA1, positive PCA2 block is evident for miR-127, miR-133a, miR-145, miR-146b, miR-16, miR-221 and miR-28. These have PCA1 from ~+5 to +16 and PCA2 broadly positive, and in the raw data they are the set that is either maintained or increased with differentiation, e.g. miR-127, miR-221 and miR-28 rise from NonArt to D10/D21 while miR-133a, miR-145, miR-146b and miR-16 stay high with a modest shift. Together they form a stable/high-expression module, Group2.

The third set sits around PCA1 ≈ -9 to +1 with PCA2 near zero to negative. miR-106b*, miR-27a*, miR-15a, miR-182, miR-203, miR-204, miR-485-3p and miR-224 all have PCA2 ≤ +3.7 and, in most cases, PCA2 <0, with PCA1 ranging from -12 to +0.6. In the expression matrix they show the intermediate behaviour: modest down-regulation from NonArt to D10/D21 without complete loss, and they are distinct from both the extreme loss cluster and the high PCA1 stable cluster. That is a consistent transitional / low-PCA2 group, Group3.

This three-way split captures the loss cluster defined by zero D10/D21 expression and extreme negative PCA1, the high PCA1 maintained cluster, and the remaining intermediate / negative PCA2 cluster.
